newsitem.title: USA: Snow, cold seen hitting U.S. Plains next week.
newsitem.headline: Snow, cold seen hitting U.S. Plains next week.

text.p: A winter storm will likely blanket the southern and central U.S. Plains with snow early next week, followed by bitterly cold temperatures, weather forecasters said Thursday.

"There's going to be a major winter storm developing early next week in the Southwest (United States), which could affect all of the southern and central Plains, followed by bitter arctic air," said Dave Dusik, meteorologist with The Weather Center Co in Kansas City.
"It looks like even as early as Monday, we could have something big going on in Kansas and Oklahoma," Dusik said.
Fred Gesser, chief forecaster at Weather Express in Omaha, Neb., said that the storm would likely bring several inches of snow to the High Plains.

"We're looking at a possibility of fairly wet conditions -- three to five inches of snow -- in the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles up through the central Plains," Gesser said. "There will be heavier amounts in some areas.

Gesser said an ensuing arctic blast would likely drive temperatures in the southern and central Plains into the single digits Fahrenheit by Wednesday morning. Areas of Nebraska could see temperatures fall below zero F, he said.
"The important part is that it's going to get very, very cold during and after the storm," Dusik said.
Gesser said it was still unclear how the storm would progress after hitting the Plains. He said the most recent meteorological models showed the storm following a course from Amarillo to Chicago.
"It's not only going to affect the cattle, it's going to affect the piggies out in Iowa, with single-digit lows likely in much of Iowa by Thursday morning," Gesser said.
